reason: Even with infinite Ramsey and elementary finite ordinal arithmetic allowed, the proof must construct a hierarchical coefficient-separated full ordinal copy, encode every admissible coefficient pattern into a finite vector coloring, and prove a matching unavoidable-pattern coloring in every full ordinal copy. The lower bound coordinates equal entries through common prefixes while retaining full residual row type. These are substantive nonroutine constructions; neither bound is a mere invocation of Ramsey. H2 is supported without a length-based H3 upgrade.
core_assessment: Independently read all source ranges 1019-1177 and definitions835-906 before the selector difficulty rationale. In the copy lemma the disjoint coefficient pools prevent cross-level equalities and split lower branches whenever higher coefficients differ. Partial subsets of a row inherit the fixed-n property by extending to n points in that infinite row. The upper bound homogenizes a finite vector indexed by all patterns, and pads each edge coefficient set using larger elements of the infinite homogeneous set. In the lower bound, same-class variables have identical higher prefixes by the contrapositive of rule5; the residual row therefore is common, and full omega^(j+1) order type supplies infinitely many full omega^j fibers, permitting a new coefficient beyond all finitely many previously chosen coefficients. Thus every canonical pattern is realized in every full copy.

The bespoke separated-copy lemma and both canonical-pattern bounds remain proved local obligations. The excluded recurrence for counting P is not needed because P is explicitly defined as a finite pattern count.

core_obligations: Construct a copy of omega^d inside an arbitrary infinite coefficient set with disjoint coefficient pools at every branch and with high-exponent coefficients smaller than lower ones.
Homogenize the finite vector of all coloring-rule realizations and show that every edge of the constructed copy is represented by a padded tuple from the homogeneous set.
Construct the coloring by canonical rule and realize every rule inside every copy of omega^d, keeping a full residual ordinal row at every assignment.

proof_roadmap.step: Inductively separate coefficient pools, giving a full ordinal copy whose edges satisfy the five canonical rules.
Encode all pattern realizations into one finite vector coloring of nd-tuples and apply infinite Ramsey.
Color by pattern and successively realize each equivalence class in any full ordinal copy; the hierarchy ensures assignments remain compatible.

This is a nonroutine canonicalization and matching extremal construction, rather than a direct Ramsey-theorem application.
